extracted.intended_audience: Patent applicants, inventors, SMEs, patent attorneys and agents dealing with the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_short: korean patent fee and document procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and eligibility rules for fee exemption/reduction, refunds, document inspection, confidentiality, and basic entitlement rules applicable to patent and utility model applicants before the Korean Intellectual Property Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for meeting exemption requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each requirement for exemption from payment of patent fees or official fees shall be met when the concerned documents are submitted. Therefore, where an applicant fell under the exemption from payment of patent fees when filing an application, but is excluded from exemption at the time of registration of the right, patent fees for the first three years shall not be exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must hold the qualifying status at the time they submit the application/request/registration documents. Eligibility that ceases between filing and registration will result in loss of exemption for the first three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects of full exemption and required evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists categories eligible for exemption (e.g., recipients under the National Basic Livelihood Security Act, persons of national merit and their surviving/bereaved families, registered disabled persons, students, military/public service personnel) and the evidential documents required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example evidential documents: one copy of qualification documents for National Basic Livelihood Security Act recipients; copy of Identification Booklet for the Physically Disabled for registered disabled persons; Certificate of Attendance for students; Certificate of Military Service for military/public service personnel. Eligibility is determined at time of submission and limited to those designated under the referenced statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial exemption framework (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial exemption from payment of application fees, examination request fees, patent fees for the first three years, or utility model registration fees shall be granted to individuals, SMEs, joint research between conglomerates and SMEs, public research organizations, technology transfer task forces, etc., under the applicable statutory provisos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different rates (e.g., 85%, 70%, 50%, 30%) apply depending on the subject and conditions; evidential documents and limits apply. The guide sets out which entity types and situations correspond to which reduction rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 85% fee reduction — specified cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of application fees, fees for a request for examination, patent fees for the first three years and utility model registration fees shall be exempted by 85% in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates qualifying categories (e.g., certain age groups such as younger than 30 but not younger than 19; 65 years old and over; cases where inventor and applicant are the same) for this highest partial exemption. Applicants must consult the listing and provide required evidential documents. (The manual lists concrete subject rows under the 85% heading.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 70% fee reduction — specified cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of application fees, fees for a request for examination, patent fees for the first three years and utility model registration fees shall be exempted by 70% in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically applies to individuals (only when the inventor is the applicant) and certain small enterprises; evidential documents for enterprises (e.g., copy of business registration certificate, documents proving SME status such as financial statements or average sales) are required where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50% fee reduction — joint research and public R&D entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of concerned fees shall be exempted by 50% in cases such as: (1) joint research between conglomerates and SMEs (application fee and examination request fee where joint research is conducted based on contract), (2) public research organizations, (3) technology transfer task forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For joint research the exemption may be limited to application and examination fees and only where the application or request for examination was filed after a stated date. Evidential documents include business registration certificates and documentation proving the small/medium enterprise and/or contract evidence; specific definitions for public research organizations and task forces are set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30% fee reduction — mid-sized firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of application fees, fees for a request for examination, patent fees for the first three years and utility model registration fees shall be exempted by 30% for mid-sized firms meeting statutory definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide a certificate of a mid-sized firm (per the Special Act with respect to growth and competitiveness of mid-sized firms). This applies to fee payment at time of the listed proceedings made after specified dates where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME and medium-enterprise classification and evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual sets detailed classification thresholds by industry for small and medium enterprises and medium enterprises (e.g., revenue/average-sales caps such as less than 12 billion won, 8 billion won, 5 billion won, etc. depending on industry). Evidential documents include a copy of business registration certificate and documents proving SME status or total assets/average sales for 3 business years (e.g., financial statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification determines eligibility and reduction rates. The guide lists industry-by-industry revenue thresholds and requires documentary proof; the appendix of the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on SMEs is referenced for business classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding for reduction — application timing and required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A person taking advantage of reduction or exemption shall state grounds for reduction/exemption and the subject for fee reduction/exemption in an application, request for examination or annual fee payment documents submitted at time of filing, making a request for examination or registration of establishment of patent right, and submit concerned evidential documents to the Commissioner of KIPO. (2) If a person failed to apply for reduction at the time of filing/request, later application for reduction shall not be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must declare the grounds and submit evidentiary documents at the time of the relevant filing/request. If evidential documents were already submitted to KIPO previously, resubmission may not be necessary; one may instead state the intention to skip resubmission and provide index information of the prior submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of patent or official fees — refundable circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees or official fees shall be refundable upon request in cases including: fees paid by mistake; all fees paid where an application is not accepted (returned); fees paid when an application is invalidated (certain fees excluded); fees paid in excess; fees in case of invalidation or disapproval of the proceeding; priority claim invalidation; following-years patent fees after a decision to revoke or invalidate a patent; various cases of withdrawal/abandonment within statutory periods resulting in refund of application or examination fees, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual enumerates detailed refundable situations (①–⑨), including time limits (e.g., withdrawal/abandonment within one month of filing for certain refunds). A request for refund of fees paid by mistake must be made by the person named on the payment receipt or by a person with power of attorney. For refunds related to revocation/invalidation decisions, the registered right holder or the name on the receipt may request the refund for subsequent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of patent-related documents (Article 216)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to obtain a certificate or certified copy or extract of a document with respect to a patent application, opposition proceedings and trial or to inspect or photocopy Patent Register entries or documents may file a request with the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board. However, the Commissioner/President may refuse inspection where the document should retain confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection will be refused for documents such as patent applications that have not been laid open or registered, appeals to final rejection for unpublished applications, or documents that may harm public health or public order/morality. Requests must use the prescribed annexed form (Form No.29 of the Enforcement Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of disclosure and removal of documents (Article 217)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents relating to patent applications, examinations, opposition proceedings, trials, retrials, or the Patent Register may only be taken out under specific conditions (e.g., for prior art searching, digitization of patent documents, or online remote working). No opinion, testimony, or answer about pending cases or decisions may be given regarding such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking documents out for other purposes is prohibited. Examiners and staff cannot give opinions or testimony about pending applications/examinations/trials or about decisions on whether to grant/refuse a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offense and penalties for divulging or misappropriating confidential information (Article 226)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any current or former employee of KIPO or the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board who divulges or misappropriates confidential information regarding an invention of a pending patent application acquired in the course of duties shall be subject to imprisonment for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 50 million won.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential information includes items to be kept confidential under the Patent Act and other relevant acts and items where considerable benefit accrues from secrecy. Divulgence includes intentional and accidental informing of third parties; misappropriation includes working the invention or filing related applications contrary to right holder's intention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executives/employees of specialized agencies deemed public officials (Article 226-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any current or former executive or employee of a specialized agency designated under Article 58(1), or an agency for digitization of patent documents, shall be deemed a current or former employee of KIPO or the Trial and Appeal Board for purposes of the offence provisions on divulging confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff of third-party agencies with access to unpublished patent content are held to the same confidentiality and criminal liability standards as KIPO employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing of already-submitted evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person conducts more than two patent-related proceedings simultaneously or consecutively and the contents of evidential documents are the same, the person can submit original copies for one proceeding and replace documents for the others by submitting copies or stating intention to reference the original documents in the attached-documents box. Referencing is allowed in specified cases (e.g., power of attorney, priority claim documents, successor-in-title, when permission/consent from third party is required, change of name/seal, representative acting for multiple parties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting copies instead of originals, the intention to reference must be stated in the attached documents box using the prescribed wording (example provided). This reduces repeated submission of identical evidence across multiple proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of evidential documents for authority of representative in certain cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents for authority of representative under Article 7 of the Patent Act do not need to be submitted in cases such as: (i) a representative who has made a notification of appointment under Article 5(2) of the Enforcement Rules and conducts proceedings within the scope of power of attorney; (ii) a representative registered for a general power of attorney under Article 5(2)(2) and acting within that scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration/notification of representative authority per the Enforcement Rules can obviate the need to re-submit proof of authority for each proceeding, provided actions stay within the registered scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to a patent (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who makes an invention or his/her successor shall be entitled to a patent under this Act; however, no employee of KIPO or the Trial and Appeal Board is entitled to a patent while in office, except by inheritance or bequest. If two or more persons jointly make an invention, they are jointly entitled to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor status or succession is the primary entitlement; special restrictions apply to KIPO/Trial employees. Joint inventors hold joint entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection when applications are filed by unentitled persons (Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is refused because the application was filed by a person not entitled to a patent, a patent application filed by a legitimate right-holder subsequent to that unentitled filing shall be deemed filed on the date of filing of the unentitled person's application — provided the legitimate right-holder's filing is not more than 30 days after the rejection date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision protects legitimate right-holders against priority loss due to filings by unentitled persons, subject to a 30-day filing limit after rejection under the referenced article.
